newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Jan 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- The head of the Civil Service K.W. Lam gave testimony to the Legislative Council select committee over the forced retirement of former director of immigration Laurence Leung, but failed to clarify the incident satisfactorily.
-- The government announced it had reached an agreement with property developers to take measures to crack down on speculation.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Winston Lord said he appreciated Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's confidence in handling the Hong Kong issue.

-- SING TAO -- Sixteen private television broadcasting stations in Linquan county in China's eastern Anhui province were shut down by the government recently to enforce rules that individuals and private organisations are only allowed to broadcast programmes from Beijing's CCTV.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The government's political consultancy office lobbied some members of the Legislative Council select committee not to pursue the case involving Leung's early retirement because it might affect the Canadian government granting visa-free entry to Special Administrative Region passport holders.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The leader of a U.S. congressional delegation to China said on Wednesday that Congress was unlikely to give permanent Most Favoured Nation trading status to Beijing until it had evaluated the trannsition of Hong Kong to China.
-- An Economist Intelligence Unit report suggested that foreign carmakers might have made a fundamental miscalculation about China's car industry.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- CITIC Pacific head Larry Yung, plagued by rumours he intended to sell off his newly acquired stake in the firm, confirmed it was a long-term investment.
